correctness.rationale: Closed signatures in a column only use it and its immediate neighbors. Nonempty signatures at column distance at least three are disjoint, so domination and pairwise separation of columns at relative distance 0, 1 or 2 suffice. Testing at the leftmost column of each pair requires precisely masks from relative positions -1 to +3. With fixed zero padding and omission of nonexistent vertices, this gives the length-four initialization, a single interior transition on four-mask states upon each append, and a fixed terminal predicate for the three remaining centers. Independent exact reproduction found 256 states and 737 interior transitions, recovered the terminal mask, and verified every component of v_6=3+1_{a=3}+wt(b)+wt(c)+wt(d) and v_13=v_6+6. A fixed min-plus transition commutes with the addition of 6, so the exact componentwise equality propagates to every n>=6, including after the same terminal minimization. Terminal bases and separate exhaustive direct enumeration of all subsets at n=2 through 9 give the initial minima (3,3,4,5,6,6,8,9,9,10,11) at widths 2 through 12. This establishes the asserted formula for every n>=2. At n=1 there are closed twins. Proposition 2 of the cited primary circular paper gives the same formula in its width domain n>=5, so the comparison is exact for cardinalities, without requiring any code to remain identifying after adding edges.
residual_risks: The finite computation is sufficient only in combination with the locality equivalence and componentwise min-plus induction; it is not extrapolation of scalar optima. The result is for closed-neighborhood radius-one identification, not total-identifying domination.

value.rationale: The optimum cardinality for the simplest open square strip is a natural exact invariant. Boundary changes can affect the code both through domination and signature collisions, so equality with the circular optimum at every comparable width is a substantive answer, not preservation of candidate solutions or just the known infinite density. The full residue correction, including the exceptional excess in two residue classes, matters for finite networks. A small componentwise certificate explains why the next seven-column block always costs the same amount; scalar numerical agreement out to a fixed length would not establish that fact.
residual_risks: No equality of optimal codebooks, classification of all minimizers, or broader strip or radius universality is proved.
